description: Test: G₂ null model — random SO(7) rotations for significance testing. Verifies: T1: Identity frame has |φ| = 7 (maximum G₂ calibration)
comments: Test: G₂ null model — random SO(7) rotations for significance testing.
Verifies:
T1: Identity frame has |φ| = 7 (maximum G₂ calibration)
T2: Random SO(7) rotations reduce |φ| below 7
T3: Mean |φ| over 100 random rotations is significantly < 7

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `arima_levinson_ar2`. ARIMA Levinson-Durbin AR(p) Coefficient Recovery Test Suite Self-contained tests validating the Levinson-Durbin Yule-Walker recursion for estimating AR model coefficients from known autocorrelation functions. description: ARIMA Levinson-Durbin AR(p) Coefficient Recovery Test Suite Self-contained tests validating the Levinson-Durbin Yule-Walker recursion for estimating AR model coefficients from known autocorrelation functions.
comments: ARIMA Levinson-Durbin AR(p) Coefficient Recovery Test Suite
Self-contained tests validating the Levinson-Durbin Yule-Walker recursion
for estimating AR model coefficients from known autocorrelation functions.
Mathematical basis: For AR(p): y[t] = φ1*y[t-1] + ... + φp*y[t-p] + ε
The Yule-Walker equations R*φ = r yield the population AR coefficients
given exact ACF. The Levinson-Durbin recursion solves this in O(p²) time.
Reference: Brockwell & Davis, "Time Series: Theory and Methods" (2002)
All functions inlined (tests cannot import stdlib).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `array_elem_field_store`. Regression test: arr[i].field = value  — store into a field of a struct that is an element of an array-of-structs. Previously NO statement detector matched `name[idx].field = expr` (array. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Regression test: arr[i].field = value  — store into a field of a struct that is an element of an array-of-structs. Previously NO statement detector matched `name[idx].field = expr` (array
comments: Regression test: arr[i].field = value  — store into a field of a struct that
is an element of an array-of-structs.
Previously NO statement detector matched `name[idx].field = expr` (array
index at root, then a field chain): it tokenized as `ident [ .. ] . ident =`
and fell through to expression-statement handling, silently dropping the
store or segfaulting. The `name.field[i] = v` (leaf-index) path was a
different, already-handled case.
Fix in lean_single.sio: stmt_is_array_elem_field_store +
compile_array_elem_field_store_x86. Array-of-struct slots hold pointers to
heap-materialized copies, so each slot must first be populated with a whole
struct (arr[i] = S{..}) before per-field mutation.
Covers: local array root, &![T;N] ref-param root, and a nested field chain
(arr[i].inner.v). Global arrays-of-structs are a separate, pre-existing
limitation (the global subscript read path supports only esz==8/esz==1, not
inline structs), so they are out of scope here.

description: Regression test: &![T; N] bare array mutation visible to caller. Bug: when a bare array variable is passed by &! exclusive reference, mutations inside the callee via (*arr)[i] = v must be visible in the caller after return.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `array_mut_ref_bare`. Regression test: bare &![T; N] array parameter mutation visible to caller. Previously broken (JIT/codegen): when passing a bare array variable by &! exclusive reference, mutations inside the callee via `arr[i] = v` (without. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Regression test: bare &![T; N] array parameter mutation visible to caller. Previously broken (JIT/codegen): when passing a bare array variable by &! exclusive reference, mutations inside the callee via `arr[i] = v` (without
comments: Regression test: bare &![T; N] array parameter mutation visible to caller.
Previously broken (JIT/codegen): when passing a bare array variable by &!
exclusive reference, mutations inside the callee via `arr[i] = v` (without
explicit deref) were not visible to the caller because the codegen path for
arr[i] = v on a &![T;N] parameter was not distinguishing array-refs from
plain scalars and emitting a byte store instead of a qword store.
Fix in lean_single.sio: stmt_is_array_store and the primary array-read path
now check VAR_TY == 10 with inner type == 8 and set is_arr_ty = 1, causing
the correct `mov [rax + rcx*8], rdx` 8-byte store to be emitted.
This test confirms all three mutation patterns work:
1. Bare index: arr[i] = v  (was broken)
2. Explicit deref: (*arr)[i] = v  (always worked)
3. Struct wrapper: b.field[i] = v  (always worked)

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `associator_field_pentagon`. Window 6 acceptance — the associahedron K₄ (n=4 pentagon) as checked code. Encodes the plan VERDICT's hand-derivation: the order-ambiguity variance of w·x·y·z is classical operad theory, and two pentagon edges are EXACT under. It should compile and run successfully. description: Window 6 acceptance — the associahedron K₄ (n=4 pentagon) as checked code. Encodes the plan VERDICT's hand-derivation: the order-ambiguity variance of w·x·y·z is classical operad theory, and two pentagon edges are EXACT under
comments: Window 6 acceptance — the associahedron K₄ (n=4 pentagon) as checked code.
Encodes the plan VERDICT's hand-derivation: the order-ambiguity variance of
w·x·y·z is classical operad theory, and two pentagon edges are EXACT under
the octonion composition norm ‖ab‖ = ‖a‖‖b‖:
‖((wx)y)z − (w(xy))z‖ = ‖[w,x,y]‖·‖z‖     (edge P0–P1)
‖w((xy)z) − w(x(yz))‖ = ‖w‖·‖[x,y,z]‖     (edge P3–P4)
No new mathematics, no GPU kernel — the "novelty" reduces to the associator
norm scaled by composition. This test makes that reduction machine-checked.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `associator_variance_mc`. β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:. It should compile and run successfully.
description: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

description: Smoke test: cross-compilation target flag parsing and codegen dispatch. The Mach-O (write_macho_x86 / write_macho_arm64) and PE/COFF (write_pe) backends were implemented but previously undocumented as "not yet wired".  They are in fact
comments: Smoke test: cross-compilation target flag parsing and codegen dispatch.
The Mach-O (write_macho_x86 / write_macho_arm64) and PE/COFF (write_pe) backends
were implemented but previously undocumented as "not yet wired".  They are in fact
dispatched by the codegen driver in main() based on TARGET_OS / TARGET_ARCH:
--target x86_64-linux   → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_elf()       (default)
--target aarch64-linux  → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_elf_arm64()
--target x86_64-macos   → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_macho_x86()
--target aarch64-macos  → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_macho_arm64()
--target x86_64-windows → TARGET_OS=3, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_pe()
This file is a minimal Sounio program that compiles and runs correctly on Linux
(the host platform).  The cross-compilation targets require running the produced
binary on the corresponding OS; the compiler itself will emit a valid Mach-O or
PE/COFF file when invoked with the appropriate --target flag.
To manually verify cross-compile flag acceptance:
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.macho --target x86_64-macos
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.pe    --target x86_64-windows
Both commands should succeed with exit code 0 and emit the respective binary format.

comments: Smoke test for stdlib/darwin_pbpk/compartments/coronary_smc.sio (Stage G-ε-17).
Exercises the 5%-of-heart sub-compartment carve-out under three regimes
(f_local = 0.30 cypher default, 0.00 systemic-only, 1.00 local-only) and
asserts two distinct invariants:
(a) Mass-balance across the routing fork (load-bearing): the deposited
mass into coronary_smc plus the systemic mass routed through blood
equals the rate-based release integral exactly — the splitter must
not leak. Checked at 1e-9 relative tolerance against the same
rectangle-rule integral both sides consume.

within 1e-9 of f_local. Confirms routing semantics.
The analytical Higuchi cumulative K_H · √t is a third reference point;
the rectangle-rule integral drifts ~0.5 % below it because the rate
formula caps the t→0 singularity. Smoke asserts the two integrals agree
to within 1 % (an integration-method drift, not a routing issue).
The dissertation §4.5.3 footnote points at this test as the routing-
integrity gate for the 5%-mass carve-out and the Cypher f_local = 0.30
claim.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk14_hessian`. tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk14_hessian.sio End-to-end demonstration of the second-order GUM Hessian propagator. Two halves:. It should compile and run successfully.
description: tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk14_hessian.sio End-to-end demonstration of the second-order GUM Hessian propagator. Two halves:
comments: tests/run-pass/dissertation_pbpk14_hessian.sio
End-to-end demonstration of the second-order GUM Hessian propagator.
Two halves:
(1) Synthetic-output residual proof.  For a controlled non-linear
endpoint y = a · x², the analytic variance is closed-form.  We
compute it three ways: ground truth, GUM 1st order (Jacobian),
GUM 2nd order (Jacobian + Hessian correction).  The acceptance
check is |GUM_2nd − truth| < |GUM_1st − truth| — the dissertation
claim that the 2nd-order term moves the GUM estimate toward the
true variance for non-linear outputs.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk28_confidence_gate`. PBPK28 rapamycin priors carried as Knowledge<f64> with literature ε. It should compile and run successfully.
description: PBPK28 rapamycin priors carried as Knowledge<f64> with literature ε.
comments: These are the real rapamycin priors from stdlib/darwin_pbpk/epistemic_pbpk28.sio
(ep28_rapamycin_priors), where confidence was a plain f64 the type system could
not see. Carried as Knowledge<f64, ε> they become first-class: the ε flows into
the EpistemicComplete gate, so a function cannot claim more confidence than its
weakest input supports.
cl_hepatic ε=0.65 (Jiao/Zhang 2009 pop-PK, CV≈38%)
fu_plasma  ε=0.72 (Schreiber 1991, CV≈25%)
kp_liver   ε=0.60 (Valoteau 1996, CV≈25%)
kp_adipose ε=0.40 (capped model, CV≈40%)   ← the weakest evidence
Gate semantics (per-token, NOT combined): `with Epistemic(N)` requires EVERY
input expression to individually carry confidence ≥ N. It does NOT certify the
propagated/combined confidence of the result (that compounds far lower). So the
maximum satisfiable N is the WEAKEST single prior, kp_adipose ε=0.40 → 400:
verified that Epistemic(400) compiles but Epistemic(401) already rejects (and
Epistemic(650) flags both kp_adipose and kp_liver). This is the type system
refusing to let any under-evidenced input enter a high-confidence claim.

description: DISSERTATION PBPK28 PARITY REFERENCE — DEGENERATE (V_v→0, PS→∞) Companion to website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs and the parity gate at scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh (Case 2: asymptotic reduction
comments: DISSERTATION PBPK28 PARITY REFERENCE — DEGENERATE (V_v→0, PS→∞)
Companion to website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs and the parity gate at
scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh (Case 2: asymptotic reduction
of PBPK28 → PBPK14 well-stirred).
Degenerate configuration:
vasc_frac_at(i) = 1e-3 ∀ organs (vs 0.019–0.282 in the literature ref)
ps_at(i)        = lit_PS_i × 1e4   (drives PS-coupling instantaneous)
At these parameters CN's A-stability is essential — explicit RK4 in the
slow operator would require dt ~ 1e-7 h for kidney/lung; CN integrates
stably at dt = 0.001 h.
CORRECTED asymptotic claim (G-α-β math correction):
PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞) does NOT reduce to PBPK14 well-stirred. It
reduces to a *1-state quasi-steady-state (QSS) model*:
V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release,
V_eff = V_b + Σ V_i · Kp_i
C_v_i = C_b instantly; C_t_i = Kp_i · C_b instantly.
PBPK14 well-stirred sits BETWEEN PBPK28-lit (finite PS, finite V_v) and
PBPK28-degenerate (V_v→0, PS→∞). The three models form a hierarchy in
model-form complexity; PBPK14 is the *intermediate* approximation where
tissue redistributes instantly *within* an organ but blood-to-tissue
transport remains rate-limited by Q. PBPK28-degenerate additionally
assumes blood-to-tissue transport is also instantaneous.
This file remains useful as: (a) the target trajectory for the
fully-coupled CN A-stability proof at extreme stiffness, and (b) the
numerical demonstration that PBPK28-degenerate matches the 1-state QSS
limit (asymptotic verification of the model-reduction theorem).
Quantitative match against the 1-state QSS limit at literature
parameters provides the Type B model-form uncertainty contribution per
JCGM 100:2008 §4.3 (the G-α-γ follow-up will emit benchmarks/pbpk/
model_form_uc.csv from these comparisons).
Model: permeability-limited PBPK, 14 organs × {vascular, interstitial}.
V_v,i · dC_v,i/dt = Q_i·(C_blood - C_v,i) - PS_i·(C_v,i - C_t,i/Kp_i)
V_t,i · dC_t,i/dt = PS_i·(C_v,i - C_t,i/Kp_i)
V_b   · dC_b/dt   = sum_i Q_i·(C_v,i - C_b) - cl_hep·C_b
Integrator: fully-coupled Crank-Nicolson on the 27-state PBPK28 system —
no operator splitting. PS coupling and Q transport integrated implicitly in
one CN step via per-organ Schur-complement elimination + scalar reduction
for C_blood. A-stable, 2nd-order, no splitting-induced bias.
Compartment indexing matches website/src/components/dissertation/compartments.ts:
0=blood 1=liver 2=kidney 3=brain 4=heart 5=lung 6=muscle 7=adipose
8=gut   9=skin  10=bone   11=spleen 12=pancreas 13=other
Bolus 0.05 mg into blood (C_blood(0) = 0.01 mg/L). cl_hep = 12.4 L/h. Stent off.
Twelve log-spaced sample times. Emits PARITY|t / PARITY|i / PARITY|cv / PARITY|ct
/ PARITY|cavg records — the gate joins on (t, i) and compares against the
Node runner's identical output.

Closed-form quasi-steady-state limit of PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞):

1-state QSS model. PBPK14 well-stirred is the *intermediate* model where
within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS
with monotonically decreasing model-form complexity. Discrepancies

//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout-contains: PASS
//
// Native-stage mirror for the F1 Moufang/alternativity smoke. The original
// import-bearing program is parked under tests/madaros/ocssm_imported/.

fn embed_axis(hash: i64) -> i64 {
    let r: i64 = hash - (hash / 7) * 7
    return 1 + r
}

fn embed_into(hash: i64, out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    out[0] = 0.6
    out[embed_axis(hash) as usize] = 0.8
}

fn oct_mul(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var r0 = a[0] * b[0]
    r0 = r0 - a[1] * b[1]
    r0 = r0 - a[2] * b[2]
    r0 = r0 - a[3] * b[3]
    r0 = r0 - a[4] * b[4]
    r0 = r0 - a[5] * b[5]
    r0 = r0 - a[6] * b[6]
    r0 = r0 - a[7] * b[7]
    out[0] = r0

    var r1 = a[0] * b[1] + a[1] * b[0]
    r1 = r1 + a[2] * b[3] - a[3] * b[2]
    r1 = r1 + a[4] * b[5] - a[5] * b[4]
    r1 = r1 - a[6] * b[7] + a[7] * b[6]
    out[1] = r1

    var r2 = a[0] * b[2] + a[2] * b[0]
    r2 = r2 - a[1] * b[3] + a[3] * b[1]
    r2 = r2 + a[4] * b[6] - a[6] * b[4]
    r2 = r2 + a[5] * b[7] - a[7] * b[5]
    out[2] = r2

    var r3 = a[0] * b[3] + a[3] * b[0]
    r3 = r3 + a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1]
    r3 = r3 + a[4] * b[7] - a[7] * b[4]
    r3 = r3 - a[5] * b[6] + a[6] * b[5]
    out[3] = r3

    var r4 = a[0] * b[4] + a[4] * b[0]
    r4 = r4 - a[1] * b[5] + a[5] * b[1]
    r4 = r4 - a[2] * b[6] + a[6] * b[2]
    r4 = r4 - a[3] * b[7] + a[7] * b[3]
    out[4] = r4

    var r5 = a[0] * b[5] + a[5] * b[0]
    r5 = r5 + a[1] * b[4] - a[4] * b[1]
    r5 = r5 - a[2] * b[7] + a[7] * b[2]
    r5 = r5 + a[3] * b[6] - a[6] * b[3]
    out[5] = r5

    var r6 = a[0] * b[6] + a[6] * b[0]
    r6 = r6 + a[1] * b[7] - a[7] * b[1]
    r6 = r6 + a[2] * b[4] - a[4] * b[2]
    r6 = r6 - a[3] * b[5] + a[5] * b[3]
    out[6] = r6

    var r7 = a[0] * b[7] + a[7] * b[0]
    r7 = r7 - a[1] * b[6] + a[6] * b[1]
    r7 = r7 + a[2] * b[5] - a[5] * b[2]
    r7 = r7 + a[3] * b[4] - a[4] * b[3]
    out[7] = r7
}

fn oct_associator(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], c: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var ab: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var ab_c: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var a_bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_mul(a, b, &!ab)
    oct_mul(&ab, c, &!ab_c)
    oct_mul(b, c, &!bc)
    oct_mul(a, &bc, &!a_bc)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = ab_c[i as usize] - a_bc[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn norm_sq(v: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 {
    return v[0]*v[0] + v[1]*v[1] + v[2]*v[2] + v[3]*v[3]
         + v[4]*v[4] + v[5]*v[5] + v[6]*v[6] + v[7]*v[7]
}

fn alt_stat_sq(x: &[f64; 8], y: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var assoc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_associator(x, x, y, &!assoc)
    let den_sq: f64 = norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(y)
    if den_sq < 0.0000000000000001 { return 0.0 }
    return norm_sq(&assoc) / den_sq
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var hashes: [i64; 8] = [100, 200, 100, 300, 200, 400, 300, 500]
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < 8 {
            if hashes[i as usize] == hashes[j as usize] {
                var x: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                var y: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                embed_into(hashes[i as usize], &!x)
                embed_into(701 + i + j, &!y)
                sum = sum + alt_stat_sq(&x, &y)
                count = count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var ok: i64 = 1
    var stat_sq: f64 = 0.0
    if count > 0 { stat_sq = sum / (count as f64) }
    if count == 0 { ok = 0 }
    if stat_sq >= 0.000000000000000000000001 { ok = 0 }

    if ok == 1 { print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }
    return 0
}

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `ffi_integer_return`. extern "C" integer returns must use RAX, not XMM0. On x86-64 System V ABI: - Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX. It should compile and run successfully.
description: extern "C" integer returns must use RAX, not XMM0. On x86-64 System V ABI: - Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX.
comments: extern "C" integer returns must use RAX, not XMM0.
On x86-64 System V ABI:
- Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX.
- Float-returning C functions (f64) return in XMM0.
Sounio's internal convention carries all values (including f64) as
bit-patterns in RAX.  When we call an extern "C" fn that returns
an integer, RAX is already correct — no fixup is needed.
The bug was that strip_extern_blocks() discarded extern "C"
declarations entirely, causing callers to receive xor-eax-eax (0)
via the undefined-variable fallback, so pid was always 0.
The fix: strip_extern_blocks() now parses each extern "C" fn decl
and emits a Sounio stub that calls the correct platform mechanism
(syscall for integer-returning OS functions; native impl for math).
The stub returns its result in RAX — the Sounio calling convention —
so the return-register dispatch is always correct.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `g2_bridge_pipeline`. Test: G₂ bridge pipeline — end-to-end from adjacency matrix to G₂ invariants. Simulates the full pipeline: 1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes). It should compile and run successfully.
description: Test: G₂ bridge pipeline — end-to-end from adjacency matrix to G₂ invariants. Simulates the full pipeline: 1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes)
comments: Test: G₂ bridge pipeline — end-to-end from adjacency matrix to G₂ invariants.
Simulates the full pipeline:
1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes)
2. Compute graph Laplacian
3. Extract 7 eigenvectors via deflated power iteration
4. Map eigenvectors to octonion basis (ψ_k ↔ e_k)
5. Compute G₂ 3-form on the eigenvector frame
6. Compute SU(3) branching quality
7. Run null model (random SO(7) rotations)
8. Compare observed vs null → p-value estimate
Verifies:
T1: Pipeline produces a finite G₂ 3-form value
T2: SU(3) quality is in [0, 1]
T3: Null distribution has lower mean |φ| than observed
T4: Eigenvectors are valid (orthogonal, unit norm)
T5: Associator deviation field computable on extracted frame
T6: Full pipeline completes without crash

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gradient_descent_from_compiler`. sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio. β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the. description: sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio. β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
comments: sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio.
β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
gradient of y with respect to each uncertain input x_k, computed by
the compiler at emit-time via forward-mode automatic differentiation.
We expose this via the new `sensitivity_of(y, k)` builtin. That turns
Sounio — a language originally designed for epistemic typed computing —
into an automatic-differentiation language.
To prove it: minimize L(x) = (x − 3)² by gradient descent, using the
compiler's sensitivity as the gradient. No external library. No manual
derivative. The compiler knows dL/dx because it computed it while
emitting the code.
Starting x = 0. Learning rate 0.1. 30 iterations.
Expected: x → 3.0, L → 0.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gtt_body_precision_param_usage`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-4 regression. Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology (conservative upper bound).  For. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-4 regression. Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology (conservative upper bound).  For
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-4 regression.
Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology
(conservative upper bound).  For
fn proj_a(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a }
let r = proj_a(k0.value, k1.value)
week-3 left EXPR_CH_SET(r) = {ch0, ch1} even though the body reads
only its first parameter.  Week-4 introduces body-level precision:
the compiler walks the callee's return expression, records the set
of parameter indices it actually depends on into FN_USED_PARAMS[fi],
and at each call site unions only those B9_ARG_CH_SET slots.  The
declared channel set becomes EXPR_CH_SET(r) = {ch0} — tight.
This test is the positive canary: the hessian query that remains
inside the tightened set (H_{0,0}) still type-checks and runs.  The
counterpart compile-fail test (gtt_body_precision_unused_param_refused)
verifies that the out-of-topology query (H_{1,1}) is now refused.
my_sum / my_square from the week-3 regression continue to type-check
under body-precision: my_sum's body references both params (union of
operand topologies = union of both args); my_square uses only one
arg (and only has one), so the tightened set matches what week-3
happened to produce by accident.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gtt_if_arm_union`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-6 stage-2 regression (if-arm union). Before this fix, `compile_primary`'s if-expression path (line ~15889) compiled both arms but did NOT propagate EXPR_CH_SET through them —. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-6 stage-2 regression (if-arm union). Before this fix, `compile_primary`'s if-expression path (line ~15889) compiled both arms but did NOT propagate EXPR_CH_SET through them —
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-6 stage-2 regression (if-arm union).
Before this fix, `compile_primary`'s if-expression path (line ~15889)
compiled both arms but did NOT propagate EXPR_CH_SET through them —
each arm's compilation overwrote EXPR_CH_SET, so the result carried
only the last-compiled arm's topology (usually the else arm).
Concretely, for
let k0 = measure(...)
let k1 = measure(...)
let r = if flag { k0.value } else { k1.value }
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)
pre-fix left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (else arm's), and the query
H_{0,0} was REFUSED at type-check because channel 0 was not in the
set — a real soundness hole.
Post-fix: EXPR_CH_SET = cond_ch_set | then_ch_set | else_ch_set.
Both H_{0,0} and H_{1,1} queries are accepted; the runtime value
depends on which arm actually ran (shadow channels aren't
path-sensitive at Phase-1 level, but topology tracking is now
correctly a conservative upper bound).
The theorem this commit catches up to: `Typing.tIf` in
formal/GradientTopology.lean §3 concludes at `Sc ∪ (S1 ∪ S2)`, which
`gtt_sound` proves is a sound runtime-footprint upper bound.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-9 indirect-call regression. Open item #2 from formal/GradientTopology.lean §7c: closure / fn-ref indirect calls were leaking the last `compile_or()` arg's
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-9 indirect-call regression.
Open item #2 from formal/GradientTopology.lean §7c: closure / fn-ref
indirect calls were leaking the last `compile_or()` arg's
EXPR_CH_SET / EXPR_PARAM_USED unchanged.  A 2-arg fn-ref dispatched
indirectly with args carrying ch[0] and ch[1] would leave EXPR_CH_SET
= {ch1}, and `hessian_of(f(x,y), 0, 1)` would be REFUSED at type-check

Week-9 unions B9_ARG_CH_SET[0..min(argc,16)] for indirect calls

same saturating widen at argc ≥ 16 as week-8 stage 2.  This test
pins down acceptance of the (0,1) and (1,0) cross-pairs.
Runtime value is silent zero (inter-procedural shadow propagation

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural). Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/ multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural).
Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/
multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
union topology across user-defined function calls — the return
inherited only the *last* argument's channel set.
Concretely, for
fn my_sum(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a + b }
let x = k0.value   // channel 0
let y = k1.value   // channel 1
hessian_of(my_sum(x, y), 0, 1)
week-2 left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (only y's topology), and the query
H_{0,1} was REFUSED at type-check because channel 0 was not in the set.
Week-3 unions the channel sets of every argument into the return
topology (conservative upper bound, matching the atan2/pow discipline).
The same program now type-checks.  The runtime value is 0.0 because
inter-procedural SSHADOW propagation is not yet wired — topology
tracking and shadow tracking are orthogonal concerns.  This test
asserts that the type checker accepts the query; the shadow pipeline
is covered by epistemic_hessian_*.
Single-arg fns (my_square below) were correct by accident pre-fix and
continue to work — union of one set is itself.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (loop snapshot/union). Before this fix, a var mutated inside a while loop would have its VAR_CH_SET frozen at the pre-loop state (or emptied if only set in the loop body) because
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (loop snapshot/union).
Before this fix, a var mutated inside a while loop would have its VAR_CH_SET
frozen at the pre-loop state (or emptied if only set in the loop body) because
the snapshot+union was missing.  After the fix:
1. VAR_CH_SET is snapshotted before the loop runs (so 0-iteration loops
preserve pre-loop topology).
2. Post-body topology is unioned with the snapshot at loop exit (so a
variable that gains channels inside the loop retains both the pre-loop
and post-loop channels — sound conservative upper bound).
This test uses a 1-iteration loop so the body definitely runs, and verifies
that the channel gained in the loop body is present in the post-loop topology.

Concretely, for
let k0 = measure(...)
let k1 = measure(...)
let opt: Option<i32> = Some(7)
let r = match opt {
Some(_) => k0.value,   // channel 0
None    => k1.value,   // channel 1
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)
pre-fix left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (last-compiled arm's), and H_{0,0}
was REFUSED at type-check — a real soundness hole parallel to the
week-6 `if`-arm leak.
Post-fix: EXPR_CH_SET = match_scrut_ch_set | match_arms_ch_union.
All three of H_{0,0}, H_{1,1}, H_{0,1} accepted.
Theorem this commit catches up to: `Typing.tMatch` in

(week-7 stage 1, commit 58f14d44), which `gtt_sound` proves is a

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-8 regression (n-ary surface). Week-3 unioned channel topology across binary user-fn calls (gtt_interprocedural_topology.sio).  Week-4 added body-precision
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-8 regression (n-ary surface).
Week-3 unioned channel topology across binary user-fn calls
(gtt_interprocedural_topology.sio).  Week-4 added body-precision
filtering via FN_USED_PARAMS.  Week-5 introduced Lean's Expr.callN
+ gtt_sound_body_callN soundness.  The compiler-side variadic
iteration over B9_ARG_CH_SET[16] has been live since week-3, but
was only validated at arity 2.  This test locks in arities 3..5
to prove the union scales smoothly across the per-arg slot table.
Concretely, for
fn my_sum3(a, b, c) -> f64 { a + b + c }
let x = k0.value   // channel 0
let y = k1.value   // channel 1
let z = k2.value   // channel 2
hessian_of(my_sum3(x, y, z), 0, 2)
pre-week-3 would have leaked only z's topology ({ch2}); the (0, 2)
query would have refused on missing channel 0.  Week-3's variadic
union over B9_ARG_CH_SET emits {ch0, ch1, ch2}, so every cross-pair
query type-checks.  This test verifies the (0,1), (0,2), (1,2)
triangle for arity 3, and analogous coverage for arity 4 and 5.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gtt_reassignment_topology`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (scalar reassignment). Before this fix, `x = expr` (var reassignment) never wrote VAR_CH_SET — only `let x = e` declarations did (lean_single.sio:16057).  So:. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (scalar reassignment). Before this fix, `x = expr` (var reassignment) never wrote VAR_CH_SET — only `let x = e` declarations did (lean_single.sio:16057).  So:
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (scalar reassignment).
Before this fix, `x = expr` (var reassignment) never wrote VAR_CH_SET —
only `let x = e` declarations did (lean_single.sio:16057).  So:
var r = 0.0
r = k0.value    // EXPR_CH_SET = {ch0}, but VAR_CH_SET[r] stayed 0
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)  // silently returned 0.0 instead of refusing
Post-fix: the reassignment path writes VAR_CH_SET[ty_vi] = EXPR_CH_SET,
so `r` carries channel 0 and H_{0,0} is correctly accepted.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (recursion). Recursion is already handled by the week-3 conservative union: at each call site, B9_ARG_CH_SET accumulates all argument channel sets, and the
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 regression (recursion).
Recursion is already handled by the week-3 conservative union: at each
call site, B9_ARG_CH_SET accumulates all argument channel sets, and the
return value's EXPR_CH_SET is the union.  For a recursive call like
fn depth_sum(x: f64, n: i64) -> f64 { if n == 0 { x } else { depth_sum(x, n-1) } }
the call site unions the argument topology (ch0) into the return, so
`hessian_of(depth_sum(k0.value, 3), 0, 0)` is correctly accepted.
This test is the positive canary confirming recursion topology is sound.

Constants: L = 50 mm = 50e6 nm, alpha_S = 11.5e-6 /°C

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knightian_dark_matter`. Knightian Uncertainty Demo: Dark Matter Candidates Frank Knight (1921) distinguished: Risk        = unknown outcome, known probability distribution. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Knightian Uncertainty Demo: Dark Matter Candidates Frank Knight (1921) distinguished: Risk        = unknown outcome, known probability distribution
comments: Knightian Uncertainty Demo: Dark Matter Candidates
Frank Knight (1921) distinguished:
Risk        = unknown outcome, known probability distribution
Uncertainty = unknown outcome, unknown distribution (ε=⊥)
Dark matter is the canonical example of Knightian uncertainty:
- We know it exists (gravitational effects are real)
- We have zero confidence in ANY model class: WIMPs, axions,
primordial black holes, modified gravity — all have been ruled out
or are severely constrained. The hypothesis SPACE is unknown.
This is not "low confidence." This is "undefined confidence."
ε=0.0 means "known to be wrong." ε=⊥ means "model space unknown."
The Knightian distinction requires different decision theory:
Risk:        Bayesian updating, expected utility maximization
Uncertainty: Maximin strategies, robust optimization
In Sounio: KnightianMode::Undefined propagates through computation.
Any function of ε=⊥ must return ε=⊥.
The distinction is enforced by the type system, not by convention.

description: M1 functor F foundation — Knowledge<Octonion> as a single epistemic capsule. Existing run-pass `knowledge_octonion_structure.sio` carries uncertainty on each of the eight octonion *components* (`Knowledge<f64>` × 8). This test
comments: M1 functor F foundation — Knowledge<Octonion> as a single epistemic capsule.
Existing run-pass `knowledge_octonion_structure.sio` carries uncertainty on
each of the eight octonion *components* (`Knowledge<f64>` × 8). This test
pins the dual idiom that the homology-functor plan (project_octonion_homology_functor)
requires: a single `Knowledge<T>` wrapping the whole struct.
What it proves about the compiler today:
1. Parser accepts `Knowledge<Octonion>` (struct as inner type, not just f64/i64).
2. Type-checker accepts the `Knowledge { value: octonion_literal }` construction.
3. `.value` projection through a struct inner returns the struct.
4. Composing two `Knowledge<Octonion>` values via a hand-written multiplier
that does the algebra on the underlying `Octonion` (not on the Knowledge
capsule directly) lowers to ELF and runs.
What it does NOT claim: arithmetic operators (+ - * /) on `Knowledge<Octonion>`
directly — the codegen at lean_single.sio:6796 legitimately rejects struct
inner types for those operators because GUM variance propagation requires a
scalar value channel. Composition lives in user-space algebra (oct_mul) and
re-wraps via `Knowledge { value: ... }`. That is the F functor's intended shape.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_octonion_structure`. variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio β-2: Knowledge<Octonion<f64>> — first GUM variance through octonion multiplication. Demonstrates the Fano-plane structure tensor and non-commutativity via variance. It should compile and run successfully.
description: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio β-2: Knowledge<Octonion<f64>> — first GUM variance through octonion multiplication. Demonstrates the Fano-plane structure tensor and non-commutativity via variance
comments: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
β-2: Knowledge<Octonion<f64>> — first GUM variance through octonion multiplication.
Demonstrates the Fano-plane structure tensor and non-commutativity via variance
asymmetry. Based on Baez "The Octonions" Bull. AMS 39 (2002).
Fano-plane convention (positive orientation):
Reverse order -> negated. e_i*e_i = -1. e_0 = 1.
Product is computed inline (no 16-param helper) because narrow param lists are
preferred by the self-hosted compiler. Variance is sampled from c0 and d0
(first components of a*b and b*a) to avoid the 3-chain x 3-stage overflow path.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_quaternion_mekf`. Task: beta-1 (Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> with MEKF-style tangent-space cov) β-1: Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> demonstration. Compares naive ambient GUM (quaternion as 4 packed Knowledge<f64> on R^4). It should compile and run successfully.
description: Task: beta-1 (Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> with MEKF-style tangent-space cov) β-1: Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> demonstration. Compares naive ambient GUM (quaternion as 4 packed Knowledge<f64> on R^4)
comments: Task: beta-1 (Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> with MEKF-style tangent-space cov)
β-1: Knowledge<Quaternion<f64>> demonstration.
Compares naive ambient GUM (quaternion as 4 packed Knowledge<f64> on R^4)
against the spirit of MEKF/LIEKF: a nominal unit quaternion with a
tangent-space (so(3)) error covariance. The former wastes a degree of
freedom on the unit-norm constraint and couples unrelated directions; the
latter tracks uncertainty in the 3-DoF small-angle error.
Witness: non-commutativity of the Hamilton product. The mean obeys
|q1*q2| = |q2*q1| = |q1||q2| (composition), but the GUM variance on the
vector components is NOT symmetric under order reversal, because the
partial derivatives of (w,x,y,z) = q1*q2 w.r.t. each input component are
a function of the OTHER operand, which differs between q1*q2 and q2*q1.
References:
- Markley, F.L. "Attitude Error Representations for Kalman Filtering"
J. Guidance, Control, and Dynamics 26(2), 2003. (MEKF)
- Barrau, A.; Bonnabel, S. "The Invariant Extended Kalman Filter as
a Stable Observer" IEEE TAC 62(4), 2017. (LIEKF)
- Shuster, M.D. "A Survey of Attitude Representations" J. Astro. Sci.
Why naive ambient GUM fails for rotations:
- q lives on S^3 in R^4 (unit-norm constraint w^2+x^2+y^2+z^2 = 1).
- Packing 4 independent Knowledge<f64> ignores the constraint; the
covariance ellipsoid leaks off the manifold.
- MEKF encodes uncertainty as dtheta in R^3 (so(3)), so P is 3x3
and stays on the tangent space. Here we mimic that by tracking
variance only on the 3 vector components (x,y,z) of the *error*
quaternion, treating w~=1 as the deterministic nominal.

comments: Regression test: method receiver inference uses declared signature, not heuristics.
Bug (pre-fix): infer_method_receiver_use used string-prefix heuristics to decide
whether a method call borrows &T, mutably borrows &!T, or moves T.  Methods whose
names did not match the heuristic patterns were treated as moves even when the
declared first parameter was &!Self, producing false-positive ownership errors or
silent miscompilation.
Fix: the method call handler now calls scan_fnsig_param_type(FN_SIG[mfi], 0) to
read the actual declared receiver type.  If SCAN_TY==10 and ref_hash_mut!=0 the
receiver is an exclusive borrow (&!Self): borrow conflict checks are enforced and
the borrow is released after the call.  No heuristic string matching is used.
This test verifies:
1. A struct method declared with &!Self can mutate state without a false positive.
2. The ownership checker permits a second &!Self call on the same variable after
the first call's ephemeral borrow has been released.
3. A &Self (shared) method may be called while no exclusive borrow is active.
4. main() returns 0 (success) when all mutations produce the expected values.

comments: Golden regression test that DISTINGUISHES a correct SRET-by-value compile

description: observe(k, y, uncertainty: s) performs normal-normal conjugate posterior contraction
comments: Lane A — native GUM->Bayes posterior contraction (M1 math-reviewed, xai/Grok 2026-05-24).
prior N(mu=10, var=4);  observe y=12 with obs var=1
var_post = var*sobs/(var+sobs) = 4*1/5 = 0.8   (< 4: contraction)
mu_post  = (mu*sobs + y*var)/(var+sobs) = (10 + 48)/5 = 11.6

description: L0 acceptance for product_nonassoc (stdlib/epistemic/propagate.sio) — the wiring that turns non-associativity into epistemic variance automatically. A scalar observable with base GUM variance 0.25 (Epistemic::measured(10, 0.5)),
comments: L0 acceptance for product_nonassoc (stdlib/epistemic/propagate.sio) — the
wiring that turns non-associativity into epistemic variance automatically.
A scalar observable with base GUM variance 0.25 (Epistemic::measured(10, 0.5)),
computed through an octonion triple:
Fano  (e1,e2,e3): associator = 0   ⇒ variance unchanged       (0.25)
non-Fano (e1,e2,e4): ‖α‖² = 4, κ=1 ⇒ variance += κ·4 = total   (4.25)
This is the join of the two theses: non-associativity does not merely get
blocked at the optimizer — it FEEDS the uncertainty budget through the
propagation engine, with certainty-of-order something you earn (Fano triple),
not assume.

description: β⁵ inter-procedural variance propagation enabled: mutable f64 vars use fixed runtime variance slots so variance_of() tracks across loop iterations and function call boundaries. EPISTEMIC ADAPTIVE ODE — FIRST IMPLEMENTATION
comments: β⁵ inter-procedural variance propagation enabled: mutable f64 vars use fixed runtime
variance slots so variance_of() tracks across loop iterations and function call boundaries.
EPISTEMIC ADAPTIVE ODE — FIRST IMPLEMENTATION
Bogacki-Shampine 3(2) with variance-aware lookbehind step control
NOVELTY: first ODE integrator that combines numerical error control with
metrological variance-growth control, using a lookbehind (post-step,
next-step) adaptive strategy:
After each in-place step:
err_norm    = |e_num| / (atol + rtol·|y|)         [numerical]
v_growth    = variance_of(y) − var_pre             [metrological]
u_ratio     = v_growth / (u_atol + u_rtol·var_pre)
dt_num   = dt · safety · (1/err_norm)^(1/3)       [3rd-order method]
dt_epist = dt · safety · (1/u_ratio)^(1/2)         [variance ~ dt²]
dt_next  = min(dt_num, dt_epist)
Why lookbehind rather than trial-and-reject:
The Sounio compiler's GUM variance propagation is reliable for in-place
mutation (var = var + …) but has limited depth for trial-then-commit
patterns in deep expression chains. Lookbehind control achieves the same
adaptive effect without rollback — the next step's dt is informed by the
current step's observed variance growth.
Method: Bogacki-Shampine 3(2) (default in MATLAB ode23)
Model:  Rapamycin 3-compartment PBPK (blood, brain, peripheral)
Ref:    JCGM 100:2008 (GUM), Bogacki & Shampine (1989)

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `reinhart_rogoff`. Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity
comments: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010 Reproducibility Demo
The 2010 R-R paper "Growth in a Time of Debt" claimed countries with
debt/GDP > 90% suffer mean growth of -0.1%, driving a decade of austerity
in the EU, US, and UK.
Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) found three compounding errors:
1. UNIT ERROR:    growth stored as percentage points but treated as fractions
2. SAMPLE ERROR:  Excel formula excluded 5 high-debt, high-growth countries
3. UNCERTAINTY:   4 country-observations — result was within noise floor
Corrected result: +2.2% growth (not -0.1%). The threshold claim was noise.
This demo shows all three errors in Sounio's epistemic tracking:
- Units: explicit fraction/pp conversion — confusion is visible
- Provenance: excluded sample is a missing branch in the computation graph
- Uncertainty: SNR < 1 makes the "threshold effect" formally indefensible
Data sources: Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) Table 3; HAP Working Paper 322.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `reinhart_rogoff_weighted`. Reinhart-Rogoff 2010: Weighting Error + Knightian Threshold Extends the base reinhart_rogoff.sio demo with two additional failures: FAILURE 4: UNCONVENTIONAL WEIGHTING. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010: Weighting Error + Knightian Threshold Extends the base reinhart_rogoff.sio demo with two additional failures: FAILURE 4: UNCONVENTIONAL WEIGHTING
comments: Reinhart-Rogoff 2010: Weighting Error + Knightian Threshold
Extends the base reinhart_rogoff.sio demo with two additional failures:
FAILURE 4: UNCONVENTIONAL WEIGHTING
R-R weighted by equal country weight instead of country-year weight.
New Zealand's single catastrophic year (1951, -7.6%) was weighted
the same as the UK's 19 years of data. This is indefensible:
one outlier year dominated the average.
FAILURE 5: KNIGHTIAN THRESHOLD CLAIM
The claim "90% debt/GDP causes negative growth" is not a measurement
with reducible uncertainty. It is a causal claim about economic
mechanism. The hypothesis SPACE is unknown. This is Knightian
uncertainty (ε=⊥): no amount of data fixes it without a causal model.
Data sources: Herndon, Ash, Pollin (2013) Table 3; HAP Working Paper 322.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `sedenion_zero_divisor`. variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio Sedenion zero-divisor confidence-collapse demonstration. Classical Moreno (1998) / Smith (1995) result: the sedenion algebra S. It should compile and run successfully.
description: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio Sedenion zero-divisor confidence-collapse demonstration. Classical Moreno (1998) / Smith (1995) result: the sedenion algebra S
comments: variance_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
Sedenion zero-divisor confidence-collapse demonstration.
Classical Moreno (1998) / Smith (1995) result: the sedenion algebra S
(dimension 16, the Cayley-Dickson double of the octonions) loses
alternativity and contains ZERO DIVISORS — non-zero a, b in S with
a*b = 0. The stdlib uses the canonical example
satisfying a*b = 0 under the standard Cayley-Dickson sign convention
(verified against stdlib math::sedenion).
CONFIDENCE-COLLAPSE EVENT
When the four scalar coefficients (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) carrying
the zero-divisor pair are themselves uncertain, the algebraic identity
a*b = 0 produces an output whose mean is exactly zero but whose GUM
variance is strictly positive. The signal-to-noise ratio formally
collapses: |E[a*b]| = 0, var(a*b) > 0.
This is the epistemic singularity Sounio is uniquely positioned to
detect at the type/effect level. A first-order GUM analysis around the
zero-divisor locus is performed below by hand-deriving two output
components of the sedenion product and tracking variance through the
scalar arithmetic shadow buffer.

    print_int(jns_disp)

// Build a main that loads f64 1.5 into rdi and calls print_f64, then exit(0)
fn emit_main(code: CodeBuffer, print_f64_off: i64) -> CodeBuffer with Mut {
    var c = code
    // mov rax, IEEE754(1.5) = 0x3FF8000000000000
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0xf8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3f)
    // mov rdi, rax
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0x89); c = emit_byte(c, 0xc7)
    // call print_f64 (rel32)
    let call_site = c.len
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xe8)
    let rel = print_f64_off - (call_site + 5)
    c = emit_byte(c, rel & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 8) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 16) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 24) & 0xFF)
    // mov edi, 0 (exit code)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xbf); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // mov eax, 60 (sys_exit)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3c); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // syscall
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x0f); c = emit_byte(c, 0x05)
    c
}

fn emit_u16(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn emit_u32(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn emit_u64(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 4) as usize] = ((v >> 32) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 5) as usize] = ((v >> 40) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 6) as usize] = ((v >> 48) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 7) as usize] = ((v >> 56) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Build code: print_f64 at offset 0, then main stub
    var code = code_buffer_new()
    code = ast_emit_print_f64_builtin(code)
    let main_off = code.len
    code = emit_main(code, 0)  // print_f64 is at code offset 0

    let code_size = code.len
    let vaddr_base: i64 = 0x400000
    let code_file_off: i64 = 0x80  // After ELF header (64 bytes) + 1 program header (56 bytes) = 120 = 0x78, round up
    let entry_vaddr = vaddr_base + code_file_off + main_off

    // Build minimal ELF64 header
    var elf: [i8; 4096] = [0; 4096]

    // ELF magic: 7f 45 4c 46
    elf[0 as usize] = 0x7f as i8
    elf[1 as usize] = 0x45 as i8  // E
    elf[2 as usize] = 0x4c as i8  // L
    elf[3 as usize] = 0x46 as i8  // F

    // EI_CLASS=2 (64-bit), EI_DATA=1 (LE), EI_VERSION=1, EI_OSABI=0
    elf[4 as usize] = 2 as i8
    elf[5 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[6 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[7 as usize] = 0 as i8

    // e_type=2 (ET_EXEC), e_machine=0x3E (x86-64)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 16, 2)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 18, 0x3E)
    // e_version=1
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 20, 1)
    // e_entry
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 24, entry_vaddr)
    // e_phoff = 64 (right after ELF header)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 32, 64)
    // e_shoff = 0 (no section headers)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 40, 0)
    // e_flags = 0
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 48, 0)
    // e_ehsize = 64
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 52, 64)
    // e_phentsize = 56
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 54, 56)
    // e_phnum = 1
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 56, 1)
    // e_shentsize = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 58, 0)
    // e_shnum = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 60, 0)
    // e_shstrndx = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 62, 0)

    // Program header (LOAD) at offset 64
    // p_type = 1 (PT_LOAD)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 64, 1)
    // p_flags = 5 (PF_R | PF_X)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 68, 5)
    // p_offset = 0
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 72, 0)
    // p_vaddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 80, vaddr_base)
    // p_paddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 88, vaddr_base)
    // p_filesz = code_file_off + code_size
    let total_file = code_file_off + code_size
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 96, total_file)
    // p_memsz = total_file
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 104, total_file)
    // p_align = 0x1000
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 112, 0x1000)

    // Copy code bytes into ELF at code_file_off
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci < code_size {
        elf[(code_file_off + ci) as usize] = code.bytes[ci as usize]
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    let elf_size = code_file_off + code_size

    // Write ELF to file using VM builtin
    let wr = write_file("/tmp/sprint235_f64.elf", elf, elf_size)
    if wr < 0 {
        print("FAIL: could not write ELF\n")
        return 1
    }

    print("PASS: ELF written size=")
    print_int(elf_size)
    print(" entry=0x")
    print_int(entry_vaddr)
    print(" code=")
    print_int(code_size)
    print("\n")
    0
}

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `type_hash_3level_nesting`. Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting (closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio). Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: type-hash 3-level PASS
description: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting (closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio). Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
comments: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting
(closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio).
Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
the inner still carried the 2^50 band, so &Option<Box<Struct>> wrapped
mod 2^64 and corrupted the struct hash — field access reported
"unknown field" and shapes collided.
Post-fix: composite inners are interned (CT_INNER_HASH[4096]) and only
a small surrogate id is multiplied, keeping the encoded hash inside
[2^50, 2^51) at arbitrary depth.
This fixture exercises field access through two structurally distinct
3-level nestings simultaneously to assert they do not alias: the same
compile unit creates and reads both &Option<Box<A>> and &Option<Box<B>>.
Under the bug, the two struct hashes would collide after the ×256 wrap
(different inner structs, same wrapped surrogate), so the field offsets
would be wrong for at least one of them.

All operands are unit basis octonions (norm²=1) measured with σ=0.5 (var=0.25),
κ=1. The measurement variance of ((a·b)·c) is then identical for any triple:
so the ONLY difference between a Fano and a non-Fano triple is the structural
term the operation adds automatically:
Fano     (e1,e2,e3): ‖α‖²=0 ⇒ variance = 0.75

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `cond_indep_violation`. conditional independence violation — a variable declared independent of itself. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: E072.
description: conditional independence violation — a variable declared independent of itself
comments: This test used to be disabled, with the claim it checks written only as a
comment, because no surface syntax could produce IndepKnowledge. The type kind
existed in the checker and nothing could reach it. Now the grammar exists and
the test asserts against the compiler instead of describing what it would say.
Do not write the skip annotation in prose here: the harness matches that string
anywhere in the file, so mentioning it silently turns this test off.
A variable is never independent of itself: P(X, X) = P(X)·P(X) only in the
degenerate case. So `IndepKnowledge<f64, x, x>` asserts nothing — and asserting
nothing is exactly how an unfounded quadrature gets licensed, since the
composition law in stdlib/epistemic/graded_effects.sio grants the tighter
bound to any claim that type-checks.
The full Pearl d-separation check (Bayes Ball, causal.sio) is NOT what rejects
this. No causal graph can be declared in source yet, so nothing can discharge
a well-formed claim. What the compiler enforces here is the one rule it can
know without a graph — and it enforces it rather than assuming it.
Reference: Pearl 1995, d-separation; Bayes Ball (Shachter 1998).

description: conditional independence violation — a variable declared independent of itself

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — Phase β⁹ week-2 regression. Week-1 version of GTT rejected inline hessian_of() queries against topologies computed inline.  It could not follow topology through a
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — Phase β⁹ week-2 regression.
Week-1 version of GTT rejected inline hessian_of() queries against
topologies computed inline.  It could not follow topology through a
let-binding: `let z = x * y; hessian_of(z, 2, 3)` silently passed
because VAR_CH_SET was declared but not persisted across `let`.
Week-2 wires VAR_CH_SET at let-binding and variable load.  The
topology of `z` is now ch[0,1] at the point of the hessian_of query,
so asking for H_{2,3} is a compile-time type error.
This is the missing half of the KAS-1 discipline: the compiler
enforces channel membership regardless of whether the expression is
inlined or named.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (loop never-entered channel). The loop snapshot+union is a conservative UPPER BOUND, not an exact set. A channel that was NEVER in the expression topology before OR inside the
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (loop never-entered channel).
The loop snapshot+union is a conservative UPPER BOUND, not an exact set.
A channel that was NEVER in the expression topology before OR inside the
loop body is still absent after the loop.
Here: r starts with channel 0 ({ch0}).  Inside the loop, r is reassigned
to k1.value ({ch1}) but ONLY when a flag is true.  The loop topology
union gives r: {ch0} | {ch1} = {ch0, ch1} — channel 1 IS in the set.
However, channel 2 (from k2.value) is never assigned to r at all.
hessian_of(r, 2, 2) must be refused.

description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — scrutinee→bound-var VAR_CH_SET seeding. Without scrutinee→bound-var VAR_CH_SET seeding, the bound variable inside a match arm carries a stale 0 in `VAR_CH_SET[vb_slot]`.  When
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — scrutinee→bound-var VAR_CH_SET seeding.
Without scrutinee→bound-var VAR_CH_SET seeding, the bound variable
inside a match arm carries a stale 0 in `VAR_CH_SET[vb_slot]`.  When
arm-body code loads the bound variable, its EXPR_CH_SET becomes 0
("unknown topology" in GTT terminology), which makes the
`hessian_of` check at `compile_primary:~8598` SILENTLY SKIP the
GTT refusal — the `b7h_ch_set != 0` guard deliberately falls through
when topology is unknown.  Result: out-of-topology `hessian_of` on a
bound variable accepts incorrectly.
With the fix, the bound variable inherits the scrutinee's declared
topology (`VAR_CH_SET[vb_slot] = match_scrut_ch_set`).  Since the
scrutinee here carries topology `{ch 0}`, and we ask for
`hessian_of(v, 2, 2)` (channel 2 not in {ch 0}), the check fires
and this program is correctly REFUSED at typecheck.
This is the direct downstream guarantee of week-7 stage 1's Lean
theorem `Typing.tMatch`: `v.footprint ⊆ Sc ∪ (Ss i)` per `gtt_sound`
— a bound variable alias of the scrutinee inherits the scrutinee's
channel set.

After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x] with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:. It should fail to compile.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology). After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x] with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology).
After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x]
with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:
var r = k0.value     // r: {ch0}
r = k1.value         // r: {ch1}  (ch0 is gone)
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)  // REFUSED: channel 0 not in {ch1}
This matches the semantics of let-binding — the variable's topology
reflects its *current* value's topology, not its history.

description: Dissertation contribution: compile-time PGx confidence gate — REFUSE path. `prescribe_haloperidol` is annotated `with Confidence(750)`. Every expression inside the body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 750/1000.
comments: Dissertation contribution: compile-time PGx confidence gate — REFUSE path.
`prescribe_haloperidol` is annotated `with Confidence(750)`. Every expression
inside the body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 750/1000.
`measure(40.0, uncertainty: 20.0)` yields confidence = 1 − 20.0/40.0 = 0.5
= 500/1000, BELOW the 750 threshold.
The compiler REJECTS this program — no binary is emitted, the rejection is
enforced before any runtime check would run.
Clinical narrative: before CYP2D6 genotyping, the only available CL estimate
is the wide population-PK prior (CV ≈ 50%). The compile-time rejection prevents
prescribing haloperidol without pharmacogenomic workup — a guarantee no runtime
check can give.
This is the psychiatric analogue of tests/compile-fail/tac_compile_gate_refuse.sio
(tacrolimus, Contribution #2). Together they demonstrate that compile-time
epistemic enforcement generalises across drug classes.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `octonion_hessian_without_reassoc`. β⁸ Phase 2 compile-fail: non-associative algebra multiplication with an active AD shadow slot must be refused when the algebra lacks `reassociate: fano_selective`. description: β⁸ Phase 2 compile-fail: non-associative algebra multiplication with an active AD shadow slot must be refused when the algebra lacks `reassociate: fano_selective`. Gate location: self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio (op==19 binary section)
comments: β⁸ Phase 2 compile-fail: non-associative algebra multiplication with an active
AD shadow slot must be refused when the algebra lacks `reassociate: fano_selective`.
Gate location: self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio (op==19 binary section)
Formal proof:  formal/NonAssocHessian.lean — `refusal_is_sound`
Trigger mechanism:
`compile_primary()` resets EXPR_SSHADOW = -1 at entry, then each field
compile also resets it.  With a SINGLE-basis algebra, `OctScalar { e0: km.value }`
compiles only one field — km.value sets EXPR_SSHADOW = 0 and no subsequent
field resets it.  The struct literal returns with EXPR_TY=6, EXPR_SSHADOW=0.
That state is captured into left_sshadow = 0 before compiling the right operand.
The gate then sees:
- left_ty == 6 (algebra struct), al_is_algebra → true
- al_mul_is_associative(OctScalar_hash) == false  (alternative mul)
- has_shadow == true  (left_sshadow = 0 >= 0)
- al_reassoc_mode == 0  (no fano_selective declared)
⇒ tc_linear_violation fires → typecheck: failed → exit 1.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `potential_outcome_both_observed`. potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: E073. This example is currently marked ignored in the upstream test suite.
description: potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit
comments: The Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference (Holland 1986):
For any unit i, only ONE of {Y_i(0), Y_i(1)} can ever be observed.
Y_i(0) = outcome under control; Y_i(1) = outcome under treatment.
Sounio enforces this via linear types: PotentialOutcome<T> is consumed on observation.
Attempting to use BOTH Y(0) and Y(1) for the same unit violates the linear type constraint (E073).
This tests the PO track (Sprint 20): TyPotentialOutcome<T> as a linearly-consumed type.
The individual treatment effect ITE = Y(1) - Y(0) is unobservable for any single unit;
only the Average Treatment Effect ATE = E[Y(1) - Y(0)] can be estimated from a population.
Reference: Holland 1986, Rubin 1974, Imbens & Rubin 2015 (Causal Inference for Statistics).

description: potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `vancomycin_low_conf`. Vancomycin prescription safety: compile-time ε-bound enforcement. ASHP 2020 §8.3 mandates ε >= 0.82 before AUC-guided dosing is permitted. A dose derived solely from Cockcroft-Gault (ε=0.40, CV ~60%) is too uncertain. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: ε.
description: Vancomycin prescription safety: compile-time ε-bound enforcement. ASHP 2020 §8.3 mandates ε >= 0.82 before AUC-guided dosing is permitted. A dose derived solely from Cockcroft-Gault (ε=0.40, CV ~60%) is too uncertain.
comments: Vancomycin prescription safety: compile-time ε-bound enforcement.
ASHP 2020 §8.3 mandates ε >= 0.82 before AUC-guided dosing is permitted.
A dose derived solely from Cockcroft-Gault (ε=0.40, CV ~60%) is too uncertain.
The compiler must reject assignment to the prescription slot at compile time.
This test demonstrates that Sounio's epistemic type system prevents
under-confident prescriptions BEFORE any code runs — a hard patient-safety
guarantee that runtime checks cannot provide.
